situation: A slice shipped in two commits: one whose subject names the slice, and a precursor whose subject names the extracted component instead. The naming convention finds only the second half of the work.
expected_guard: the summary covers what could be attributed, and one line says how many commits in the range could not be tied to the slice
must_not: assign the unattributed commit to the slice on a guess
assign it on file-path overlap, which would sweep in unrelated work touching the same files
omit the count, which is the only signal that the landed view is partial
report SUMMARY-RENDERED alone, which claims a complete reconciliation
refuse to summarise — a partial landed view with its gap named is worth more than none
why_this_fixture_exists: Measured over this repo's last nine commits on 2026-09-08: four name no slice, and one of those four is a precursor belonging to a slice whose sibling commit does name it. So the convention fails on precursor commits specifically — the work a slice does BEFORE its headline change, which is exactly the work a brief is least likely to have described.
